metric.why: Announced megawatts are the leading indicator for land, power, and equipment demand. The published numbers come almost entirely from commercial research firms; this site links to who publishes them rather than republishing figures it cannot verify.
metric.definition: Capacity in permitting, planned, or under construction per market, the standard unit for comparing data center booms across regions.

reading.body:
Announced data center construction pipelines measure megawatt capacity across permitting, planned, and under-construction phases, making them the earliest signal for when land, power, and physical equipment demand will materialize.

Pipeline announcements matter because they precede actual power consumption by months or years. A megawatt announced today represents concrete commitments to land acquisition, grid interconnection studies, and supply chain orders. For AI specifically, these numbers reveal where compute infrastructure will physically exist before the servers arrive, which means they show where power constraints will next become binding before the constraint itself arrives.

The data here comes from commercial research firms rather than regulatory filings, which means it captures what vendors choose to announce rather than what permits actually require. Announced pipelines can shift, shrink, or stall. The metric does not distinguish between the stages within the pipeline, so a megawatt in early permitting carries the same weight as one under active construction. This conflates proximity to grid demand by months or even years.
